question.problem: Consider the infinite geometric series starting from ${a}_{1}=-14$  with the property $\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}=-\frac{1}{7}.$ Write the sum to infinity of the terms of this series using sigma notation.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the sequence is a geometric sequence since the ratio of any two successive terms is constant.

The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=-14,$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}=-\frac{1}{7}.
$$

Therefore, the general term ${a}_{n}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{(r)}^{n-1} \\  & =-14{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{n-1} \\  & =-14{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{-1}{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{n} \\  & =98{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }98{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$
